vehicle_mapping.yaw_rate_formula: yaw_rate = vx * kappa after step_time_s, else 0
vehicle_mapping.trajectory_formula: straight segment x = vx * t before step; circular arc x = vx * step_time + sin(yaw_rate * tau) / kappa, y = (1 - cos(yaw_rate * tau)) / kappa after step

yaw_rate.coordinate_frame: body yaw about world z, CCW positive

yaw_rate_peak_dps.reason: Kinematic ideal Ackermann should match the post-step analytic yaw-rate formula to numerical precision.

yaw_gain_dps.reason: Yaw gain is post-step yaw_rate_peak_dps divided by the front-wheel step angle (deg). Pre-v0.100 this was normalised-input (157.118); the front_deg unit (v0.100) re-expresses it per degree of inner-front-wheel angle. The angle is derived with the strategy's own symmetric-4WIS geometry (ICR lever arm L/2), not the bicycle relation.

yaw_rise_time_s.reason: The kinematic model has no steering actuator lag, so the analytic step response is instantaneous at sample resolution.

yaw_settling_time_s.reason: The kinematic response reaches the steady yaw-rate immediately after the step.

vy_peak_kmh.reason: Ideal Ackermann target has zero body-frame lateral velocity at the body origin.

speed_error_rms_kmh.reason: Kinematic model accepts the target wheel speed without actuator or tyre lag.

pose_y_peak_abs_m.reason: Continuous closed-form trajectory compared with forward-Euler pose integration; centimetre-level discretisation error is expected.

trajectory_error_rms_m.reason: Allows the known continuous-vs-discrete integration RMS difference at dt=0.005 s.

trajectory_error_peak_m.reason: Allows the known continuous-vs-discrete integration peak difference at dt=0.005 s.

limitations: Analytic reference covers kinematic ideal-Ackermann step-steer geometry only.
It intentionally excludes steering actuator lag, tyre force build-up, load transfer, suspension compliance, and measured vehicle behaviour.
It is L3 analytic-reference evidence, not external-tool or L4 measured evidence.
